rulings.challenge_claim: The verdict quotation at Jer.29.32 is glossed in English beyond the extent of the Hebrew it cites: the row splices only the opening clause of the verse yet pairs that splice with a three-clause English quotation.
rulings.grounds: Defect real, framing and severity corrected. The verdict pair splices הִנְנִ֨י פֹקֵ֜ד עַל שְׁמַעְיָ֣ה הַנֶּחֱלָמִי֮ וְעַל זַרְעוֹ֒ (oshb:Jer.29.32, byte) and pairs it with an English run that also carries “He will not have a man to dwell among this people. He won’t see the good that I will do to my people,” (web:Jer.29.32) — the renderings of לֹא יִהְיֶ֨ה ל֜וֹ אִ֣ישׁ יוֹשֵׁ֣ב בְּתוֹךְ הָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֗ה and וְלֹֽא יִרְאֶ֥ה בַטּ֛וֹב אֲשֶׁר אֲנִ֥י עֹשֶֽׂה לְעַמִּ֖י (oshb:Jer.29.32, byte for each), two clauses the spliced run does not contain. Gloss extent exceeds splice extent, so the pairing fails. First correction, the object: the English does not exceed the VERSE — every clause it carries stands inside oshb:Jer.29.32, the cited ref is right, and the English is verbatim against the staged text at web:Jer.29.32 — what it exceeds is the SPLICE, which is the defect that actually needs curing. Second, the severity: rating this below the same-class pairing gaps carried at Jer.30.5, Jer.30.12, Jer.30.17, Jer.30.18, Jer.31.1, Jer.31.2 and Jer.31.3 inverts the risk order, because those leave an English rendering uncovered while this one asserts, under a byte-tier Hebrew citation, content the cited run does not carry. Everything else in the span verifies: the other 29:32 pair, לָכֵ֞ן כֹּֽה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה (oshb:Jer.29.32, byte) against “therefore Yahweh says,” (web:Jer.29.32), is extent-clean; the word-event onset pair at 29:30 is extent-clean and byte-true; and the disclosures hold against the inventories — PE at MT 29:29, SAMEKH at MT 29:32, two paseq segs at MT 29:32 (single-witness, seg layer, count-only), no ketiv/qere note in the span.
rulings.remedy: In P10-015 boundary_rationale, re-cut the second Jer.29.32 pair so gloss extent equals splice extent: either extend the pointed run programmatically from the source bytes through לְעַמִּ֖י (oshb:Jer.29.32, byte) so it covers the two further clauses, or trim the English to “Behold, I will punish Shemaiah the Nehelamite and his offspring.” (web:Jer.29.32). Never re-key the Hebrew. Test the cure the way the original failed: every clause in the paired English must have its counterpart inside the paired Hebrew run and every clause in the run must be covered by the English; then re-collate the run at byte tier against oshb:Jer.29.32 and re-check the English verbatim against staged web:Jer.29.32 with curly pairing intact. Span, unit_type, confidence, boundary_evidence_refs and device_notes are untouched.

rulings.challenge_claim: The stated warrant that nothing between the header and the closing rubric reopens the address with a new addressee or a discourse imperative is contradicted by Jer.30.2, which the row quotes itself.
rulings.grounds: Half the challenge holds on the bytes, half does not. MT 30:2 carries כְּתָב לְךָ֗ and דִּבַּ֥רְתִּי אֵלֶ֖יךָ (oshb:Jer.30.2, byte for each) — a command form with an explicit second-person singular addressee marker, read as an imperative in the other witness, “Write all the words that I have spoken to you in a book.” (web:Jer.30.2) — while MT 30:1 carries no second-person form at all. An unqualified denial that any discourse imperative stands between the header and the rubric therefore cannot survive a form standing inside the row's own splice, and that arm of the warrant sentence is defective. The other arm is not contradicted and the challenge does not separate them: the addressee at 30:2 is the figure the header itself names, הַדָּבָר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הָיָ֣ה אֶֽל יִרְמְיָ֔הוּ (oshb:Jer.30.1, byte), so nothing NEW is addressed — the address is specified, not reopened — and the messenger formula at 30:2 carries no frame-owner change, the mouth being the same throughout. Under the ruled internal-seam classes a commissioning write-command inside a superscription is not the audience-summoning discourse frame that cuts, so the seam stands, as the challenge itself concedes. One further check the challenge did not make: the row's narrower version of the same absence, made in strongest_rejected_alternative about the 30:3/30:4 turn, is byte-true — MT 30:4 carries no speech formula, no imperative and no second-person form (oshb:Jer.30.4, byte). Disclosures verify: SAMEKH at MT 29:32 at the front seam and PE at MT 30:3 inside the span, single-witness, tier-3 weak, and no paseq seg or ketiv/qere note in the span.
rulings.remedy: In P11-001 boundary_rationale, replace the blanket absence sentence with one that names the class it denies and survives the bytes at 30:2: state that the imperative standing there is a commissioning write-command addressed to the same figure the header names, and that the messenger formula at 30:2 carries no frame-owner change, so neither reaches the internal-seam classes that cut. Test the cure the way the original failed: read the rewritten sentence back against each of Jer.30.1 through Jer.30.4 and confirm it denies no form that stands in the row's own splices. Span, unit_type, confidence, observed_substrate_signals and device_notes unchanged; no boundary change is ordered.

rulings.challenge_claim: Two items, distinct defects. (i) The unit's own opening quotation, the messenger formula the row relies on as its seam warrant, is glossed in English only from partway through the Hebrew verse spliced beside it at Jer.30.5. (ii) The declared false-positive disposition is refuted: Jer.30.8 carries the span's first second-person singular addressee, so the asserted absence of an addressee change at that turn is byte-false in both witnesses.
rulings.grounds: Both upheld; distinct defects, one mechanical and one substantive. (i) The 30:5 pair splices the whole verse including כִּי כֹה֙ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.30.5, byte) but glosses only from the cry onward, while the staged verse opens “For Yahweh says:” (web:Jer.30.5) — the formula's own English stands in the same staged verse and is left uncovered, on the single device the row cites as its opening warrant. (ii) Person marking re-derived across the span: 30:5 carries the first-person plural שָׁמָ֑עְנוּ, 30:6 the second-person plural שַׁאֲלוּ נָ֣א וּרְא֔וּ, 30:7 third person throughout, and then 30:8 carries אֶשְׁבֹּ֤ר עֻלּוֹ֙ מֵעַ֣ל צַוָּארֶ֔ךָ וּמוֹסְרוֹתֶ֖יךָ אֲנַתֵּ֑ק (oshb:Jer.30.5, oshb:Jer.30.6, oshb:Jer.30.8, byte for each), the span's first second-person singular marking, rendered the same way in the other witness, “that I will break his yoke from off your neck, and will burst your bonds.” (web:Jer.30.8). A flat denial that any addressee change marks that turn is byte-false. Two calibration points that do not disturb the finding but do bear on how strong the rival is. First, that marking is sustained to the row's own close, וְאַתָּ֡ה אַל תִּירָא֩ עַבְדִּ֨י (oshb:Jer.30.10, byte) and כִּֽי אִתְּךָ֥ אֲנִ֛י through אֲנַקֶּֽךָּ (oshb:Jer.30.11, byte for each), so this is a turn into a sustained address rather than a one-verse anomaly. Second, the 30:8 clause mixes persons in one breath, עֻלּוֹ֙ third-person beside צַוָּארֶ֔ךָ second-person (oshb:Jer.30.8, byte for each), so the turn is a person shift inside continuous divine speech, not a clean fresh address. A precision note on the framing, not a correction to the finding: the flagged word in that sentence is a restrictive adverb and is a genuine keyword false positive on its own terms; what fails is the absence clause standing beside it. Everything else verifies: no mark at MT 30:4, SAMEKH at MT 30:9, PE at MT 30:11, one paseq seg each at MT 30:8 and MT 30:11 (single-witness, count-only), no ketiv/qere; the hoy at 30:7 is the day-alas role and not a woe onset; the Jacob spelling is defective at 30:7 and twice at 30:10 (sweep: 2 token hits at Jer.30.10, 1 prefixed at Jer.30.7, skeleton, finals-normalized) against the plene form at 30:18; and all five pointed runs and all five English runs are byte-true and verbatim respectively.
rulings.remedy: Two work orders on P11-002. (1) boundary_rationale: extend the 30:5 gloss to cover the formula the splice already contains, “For Yahweh says:” (web:Jer.30.5), or trim the splice to the cry alone. Test: the paired English and the paired Hebrew must cover the same clauses; re-collate the run at byte tier against oshb:Jer.30.5 and re-check the English verbatim against staged web:Jer.30.5. (2) strongest_rejected_alternative: the sentence may no longer assert that no addressee change marks the 30:7/30:8 turn. Re-argue the rejection on grounds the bytes support — state the second-person singular entry at 30:8, weigh it against the mixed person marking inside that same clause and against the absence of any fresh speech formula there, and land the rejection on that. Test the cure the way the original failed: read the rewritten sentence back against oshb:Jer.30.7 through oshb:Jer.30.11 and confirm it denies no form standing in those verses. If the rejection cannot be re-grounded, the alternative becomes a boundary PROPOSAL — a cut at Jer.30.8 — requiring explicit owner adoption, never author work. In the same pass, disclose the second-person plural imperative pair at 30:6 or carry it in observed_substrate_signals, since the row's own rejection criteria treat imperatives as onset candidates and this one stands inside the span undeclared. If the driver changes, observed_substrate_signals, unit_type and confidence re-open with it.

rulings.challenge_claim: Two items. (i) Both of the row's load-bearing quotations, at its opening and at its close, gloss only part of the full Hebrew verse spliced beside them (Jer.30.12, Jer.30.17). (ii) The declared false-positive disposition is refuted: the exclusivity-shaped claim that nothing divides the complaint from the reversal carries no sweep and is contested by the verse-initial pivot particle at Jer.30.16 inside the span.
rulings.grounds: Item one upheld as framed; item two refined on its object. (i) The 30:12 pair splices the whole verse including כִּ֣י כֹ֥ה אָמַ֛ר יְהוָ֖ה (oshb:Jer.30.12, byte) but glosses only from the wound complaint onward, while the staged verse opens “For Yahweh says,” (web:Jer.30.12); the 30:17 pair splices the whole verse including כִּי֩ אַעֲלֶ֨ה אֲרֻכָ֥ה לָ֛ךְ וּמִמַּכּוֹתַ֥יִךְ אֶרְפָּאֵ֖ךְ נְאֻם יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Jer.30.17, byte) but glosses only the outcast clause, leaving “For I will restore health to you, and I will heal you of your wounds,” (web:Jer.30.17) uncovered. Both are real, and the 30:17 gap is load-bearing twice: the healing clause is the content the row's own close rests on AND the content its rejection of the judgment reading rests on, and both lenses reached that verse independently. (ii) The object is mis-anchored. The digits reproduce exactly on an independent re-sweep of the consonantal skeleton — the token stands in 55 verses book-wide and verse-initially in exactly 2 across MT chs 29-31, MT 29:32 and MT 30:16 (sweep: 2 verses, verse-initial, finals-normalized) — and לָכֵ֞ן (oshb:Jer.30.16, byte) does stand verse-initially at the joint. But the sentence challenged denies a fresh FORMULA, and this token is a discourse particle, not a member of any formula class: inside MT 30:12-30:17 the messenger formula stands only at 30:12 and the closure formula only at 30:17, with nothing at 30:13-30:16 (sweep: 1 verse each, span-scoped). On its own object the sentence is byte-true and is not refuted; and a six-verse span-scoped absence readable directly off the bytes is not the exclusivity class that must carry a book-wide digit. What survives is narrower and still a defect: the sentence names no swept object before asserting the absence, and the pivot particle at 30:16 is a byte-true hinge sitting at the exact joint the rejection concerns and goes undisclosed. A byte fact neither reading drew: because that particle turns the announcement at 30:16 rather than at 30:17, it argues the reversal begins one verse earlier than the rejected complaint-only grouping of 30:12-30:16 assumes, so it tells against that alternative rather than for it. Disclosures verify: PE at MT 30:11 at the front seam, SAMEKH at MT 30:17 at the close, one paseq seg at MT 30:15 (single-witness, count-only), no ketiv/qere in the span; the feminine-singular onset marking at אָנ֣וּשׁ לְשִׁבְרֵ֑ךְ (oshb:Jer.30.12, byte) is byte-real.
rulings.remedy: Two work orders on P11-003. (1) boundary_rationale: re-cut the 30:12 and 30:17 pairs so gloss extent equals splice extent — the 30:17 pair must cover “For I will restore health to you, and I will heal you of your wounds,” (web:Jer.30.17), the healing clause its own argument rests on. Test: each paired English run and its paired Hebrew run cover the same clauses; re-collate at byte tier against oshb:Jer.30.12 and oshb:Jer.30.17 and re-check both English runs verbatim against the staged web: verses. (2) strongest_rejected_alternative: name the swept object before the absence — state which formula classes were swept across Jer.30.13 through Jer.30.16 and with what digit and unit — and disclose the verse-initial pivot particle at 30:16, including that the announcement turns there. Test the cure the way the original failed: the rewritten sentence must name its swept object and unit, and must deny no device standing anywhere in Jer.30.12 through Jer.30.17 when read back against those six verses. No boundary change is ordered: span, unit_type and confidence stand.

rulings.challenge_claim: Two items. (i) The row's opening quotation and its quotation of the actively-held closing verse each gloss only part of the full Hebrew verse spliced beside them (Jer.30.18, Jer.31.1). (ii) The covenant formula at Jer.30.22 arrives on a second-person switch the row explicitly denies; the wrath coda at Jer.30.23-Jer.30.24 is an undisclosed near-twin of Jer.23.19-Jer.23.20; and the spelling contrast the row argues rests on two verses outside its own span that its evidence list does not carry.
rulings.grounds: Both upheld as distinct defects, and the recurrence arm is understated. (i) The 30:18 pair splices the whole verse including כֹּ֣ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה (oshb:Jer.30.18, byte) and glosses only from the reversal onward, while the staged verse opens “Yahweh says:” (web:Jer.30.18); the 31:1 pair splices the whole verse including בָּעֵ֤ת הַהִיא֙ נְאֻם יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.31.1, byte) and glosses only the covenant clause, leaving “At that time,” says Yahweh, (web:Jer.31.1) uncovered — on the one verse the row holds open, where that temporal phrase is half of its own stated reason for holding it. (ii) Person marking: MT 30:18-30:21 is third person throughout, אָהֳלֵ֣י יַֽעֲק֔וֹב וּמִשְׁכְּנֹתָ֖יו (oshb:Jer.30.18, byte) and אַדִּיר֜וֹ closing at נְאֻם יְהוָֽה (oshb:Jer.30.21, byte for each), and 30:22 opens וִהְיִ֥יתֶם לִ֖י לְעָ֑ם with וְאָ֣נֹכִ֔י אֶהְיֶ֥ה לָכֶ֖ם לֵאלֹהִֽים following (oshb:Jer.30.22, byte), the span's first second-person forms, rendered the same way in the other witness, “You shall be my people, and I will be your God.” (web:Jer.30.22). The flat denial of any addressee change is byte-false. (iii) The coda recurrence verifies and is stronger than claimed: the opening run הִנֵּ֣ה סַעֲרַ֣ת יְהוָ֗ה חֵמָה֙ יָֽצְאָ֔ה and the closing run עַ֛ל רֹ֥אשׁ רְשָׁעִ֖ים יָחֽוּל (oshb:Jer.30.23, byte for each), together with the run עַד עֲשֹׂת֥וֹ וְעַד הֲקִימ֖וֹ מְזִמּ֣וֹת לִבּ֑וֹ (oshb:Jer.30.24, byte), each stand in exactly 2 verses book-wide (sweep: 2 verses each, skeleton, finals-normalized), and against oshb:Jer.23.19 and oshb:Jer.23.20 all three are identical at BYTE tier, accents included, not merely consonantally; the divergences are סַ֖עַר מִתְגּוֹרֵ֑ר (oshb:Jer.30.23, byte) against וְסַ֖עַר מִתְחוֹלֵ֑ל (oshb:Jer.23.19, byte), the added חֲרוֹן֙ and the pointing of בְּאַחֲרִ֥ית הַיָּמִ֖ים (oshb:Jer.30.24, byte for each), and one extra closing word at MT 23:20. A byte-tier recurrence of that extent is texture and never a boundary driver, but it is a disclosure object and the row is silent on it. (iv) The prose argues verse 10 and verse 7, resolving to Jer.30.10 and Jer.30.7, from outside the span Jer.30.18-Jer.31.1, and neither stands in boundary_evidence_refs; the spelling substance is right — plene אָהֳלֵ֣י יַֽעֲק֔וֹב וּמִשְׁכְּנֹתָ֖יו (oshb:Jer.30.18, byte) against the defective form twice at 30:10 and, prefixed, once at 30:7 (sweep: 2 token hits at Jer.30.10 and 1 prefixed hit at Jer.30.7, skeleton, finals-normalized) — so this is a mirroring omission, not a false claim. Two byte facts neither reading drew. The coda names the divine name in the third person twice, הִנֵּ֣ה סַעֲרַ֣ת יְהוָ֗ה חֵמָה֙ יָֽצְאָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.30.23, byte) and לֹ֣א יָשׁ֗וּב חֲרוֹן֙ אַף יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.30.24, byte), immediately after the first-person clause וְאָ֣נֹכִ֔י אֶהְיֶ֥ה לָכֶ֖ם לֵאלֹהִֽים (oshb:Jer.30.22, byte) at 30:22, so 'still the same speaker' is an undisclosed shift as well as an untiered form claim — the audience does stay second-person plural, so only the speaker arm fails. And the held-open close inverts the covenant formula and flips its person: וְהֵ֖מָּה יִֽהְיוּ לִ֥י לְעָֽם at oshb:Jer.31.1 (byte) against וִהְיִ֥יתֶם לִ֖י לְעָ֑ם at oshb:Jer.30.22 (byte), third-person plural where 30:22 is second-person plural, which bears directly on the seam the row holds open and is undisclosed. Disclosures otherwise verify: SAMEKH at MT 30:17, MT 30:22 and MT 31:1, one paseq seg each at MT 30:18 and MT 30:23 (single-witness, count-only), no ketiv/qere in the span.
rulings.remedy: Four work orders on P11-004, none of them a boundary change. (1) boundary_rationale: re-cut the 30:18 and 31:1 pairs to gloss extent equals splice extent, the 31:1 pair covering “At that time,” says Yahweh, (web:Jer.31.1) since the held seam turns on that phrase. Test: paired English and paired Hebrew cover the same clauses; re-collate both runs at byte tier and re-check both English runs verbatim against the staged web: verses. (2) boundary_rationale: delete 'without any addressee change' and state the actual turn — third person through 30:21, second-person plural from 30:22 — then re-argue why that turn does not cut, on the ground that no fresh speech formula stands at 30:22. Test the cure the way the original failed: read the replacement back against oshb:Jer.30.18 through oshb:Jer.30.22; it must deny no form standing there. (3) device_notes: disclose the coda recurrence with its object, unit, digit and tier all named — byte-tier identity of the three runs against Jer.23.19-Jer.23.20, exactly 2 verses each book-wide, with the four divergence points listed — and label it texture, never a boundary driver; in the same pass disclose the third-person naming of the divine name at 30:23-30:24 beside the first-person clause at 30:22, and the person flip between 30:22 and 31:1. Test: every recurrence claim carries the tier it was verified at, and every disclosure names its swept object and unit before its digit. (4) boundary_evidence_refs: add oshb:Jer.30.7 and oshb:Jer.30.10, the two out-of-span verses the spelling contrast argues from, or drop the contrast from both boundary_rationale and device_notes. Test: every verse argued outside Jer.30.18-Jer.31.1, including bare 'verse N' mentions resolved against the span chapter, resolves to an entry in the list. The held 31:1 attachment stays open at its reduced confidence with frontier_flag_considered set; the person flip is new input for that open question and belongs in the disclosure, not in a re-span.

rulings.challenge_claim: Two items. (i) Both of the unit's first two verses are glossed in English only from partway through the full Hebrew verse spliced beside them (Jer.31.2, Jer.31.3). (ii) The declared false-positive disposition is refuted: Jer.31.2 has no addressee at all and Jer.31.3 both reports the deity in the third person and opens a feminine-singular address, so the asserted single continuous voice addressed to one figure is byte-false.
rulings.grounds: Both upheld, and they interlock rather than duplicate. (i) The 31:2 pair splices the whole verse including כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.31.2, byte) and glosses only from the wilderness clause onward, while the staged verse opens “Yahweh says,” (web:Jer.31.2) — again the uncovered element is the unit's own opening seam device. The 31:3 pair splices the whole verse including מֵרָח֕וֹק יְהוָ֖ה נִרְאָ֣ה לִ֑י (oshb:Jer.31.3, byte) and glosses only from the love clause onward, leaving “Yahweh appeared of old to me, saying,” (web:Jer.31.3) uncovered. (ii) MT 31:2 carries no second-person form anywhere: מָצָ֥א and הָל֥וֹךְ לְהַרְגִּיע֖וֹ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל (oshb:Jer.31.2, byte for each) are third person throughout, so there is no addressed figure at 31:2 for 31:3 to keep addressing. MT 31:3 then opens by naming the divine name in the third person beside a first-person singular pronoun, מֵרָח֕וֹק יְהוָ֖ה נִרְאָ֣ה לִ֑י (oshb:Jer.31.3, byte), read the same way in the other witness, and only after that clause do the feminine-singular forms אֲהַבְתִּ֔יךְ and מְשַׁכְתִּ֥יךְ (oshb:Jer.31.3, byte for each) begin. The asserted single continuous voice addressed to the same figure fails on both halves. The consistency point holds too: the same feminine-singular pointing that carries an onset warrant at אָנ֣וּשׁ לְשִׁבְרֵ֑ךְ (oshb:Jer.30.12, byte) is refused that weight here, one device read two ways within six verses. The two items interlock: the clause the quotation leaves uncovered at 31:3 is precisely the clause that falsifies the rejection sentence, so curing the pairing surfaces the evidence against the row's own stated ground. Disclosures verify: SAMEKH at MT 31:1 at the front seam, PE at MT 31:6 at the close, no paseq seg and no ketiv/qere note in the span; the 31:4 and 31:6 pairs are extent-clean, and all four pointed runs are byte-true with all four English runs verbatim.
rulings.remedy: Two work orders on P11-005. (1) boundary_rationale: re-cut the 31:2 and 31:3 pairs so gloss extent equals splice extent — the 31:3 pair must cover “Yahweh appeared of old to me, saying,” (web:Jer.31.3). Test: each paired English run and its paired Hebrew run cover the same clauses; re-collate at byte tier against oshb:Jer.31.2 and oshb:Jer.31.3 and re-check both English runs verbatim against the staged web: verses. (2) strongest_rejected_alternative: replace the continuity assertion with the bytes — no second-person form stands in 31:2, and 31:3 opens a third-person report of the divine name with a first-person singular pronoun before the feminine-singular address begins — then re-argue the rejection on a ground that survives them. Test the cure the way the original failed: read the rewritten sentence back against oshb:Jer.31.2 and oshb:Jer.31.3 and confirm it asserts no person or addressee continuity the bytes deny; and if feminine-singular onset marking is refused weight here, the refusal must rest on a ground that does not contradict the weight the same pointing is given at Jer.30.12. If the rejection cannot be re-grounded, the alternative becomes a boundary PROPOSAL — a cut at Jer.31.3 — requiring explicit owner adoption, never author work; if the driver changes, observed_substrate_signals, unit_type and confidence re-open with it.
